title: Fp prime Montgomery batch SIMD for general 64-bit primes (AVX2)
description:
## Current Generic `Fp

` Montgomery batch ops fall back to scalar element-wise loops; only `Fp<65537>` and `Fp<2^31-1>` have batch SIMD. ## Fix (AVX2 path — stays on MSRV 1.80) V3 SIMD via 32×4 limb decomposition on AVX2: split each 64-bit Montgomery operand into two 32-bit limbs, pack 4 elements per YMM, multiply with `_mm256_mul_epu32`, propagate carries explicitly. Add a `MontgomeryFns` set in `gf2-kernels-simd`. ## IFMA52 sub-task (separate dependent task — DO NOT include in this task) If the AVX2 path measures below 1.5×, open a follow-up dependent task `C3-ifma52` that: 1. Requires explicit user MSRV-bump approval per `escalation-policy.md`. 2. Adds an AVX-512 IFMA52 path (52-bit unsigned multiply-add via `_mm512_madd52lo_epu64` / `_mm512_madd52hi_epu64`) on a Rust-1.89 branch. 3. Compile-gated behind `#[cfg(all(target_arch = ..., target_feature = ...))]` with the AVX2 path as fallback. ## Per-kernel execution protocol Same as C1. Bench: `fp_specialized` + `fieldvec_dot_product`. ## Depends on I1, I2, I3, I4. ## Success criteria (AVX2 path only — IFMA52 is a separate task) - [hard] Bit-exact vs. scalar Montgomery for every prime in the existing `proofs/` test suite. - [hard] Existing Mersenne/Fermat specialisations unchanged. - [hard] Lean4 proofs still build (`./scripts/verify-lean.sh`). - [aspirational] ≥1.5× geomean over scalar fallback for at least one general 64-bit prime at the design batch size. - [hard] If aspirational misses: file the IFMA52 dependent task with the user-approval escalation; do not bump MSRV unilaterally.
